the characterization of smoke-exposed berries, and the development of a method to detect and identify VP-glycoside and non-VP glycones in smoke-exposed wine.

the development of a method for the analysis, identification, and characterization of VP-glycoconjugates in grapes and wine, with the aim to understand the chemical basis of smoke taint in grapes and wine.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this study provides the first complete method for VP-glycoside analysis in wine, including the first reported synthesis of VP-glycones.
this work has demonstrated the presence of a number of glycosides that can be elevated following exposure to smoke and that these may contribute to smoke taint in grapes and wine.
this study has demonstrated the presence of VP-glycones in smoke-exposed wine and grape berries, and has developed a comprehensive analytical methodology for their characterization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the VP-glycoside content of smoke-exposed berries is elevated and that the VP-glycerides are the most abundant VP-glycosidic derivatives.
VP-glycoside analysis is now possible, and the results can be used to improve our understanding of the smoke-taint problem in wine.
the glycosylated forms of volatile phenols are a new class of wine components that can be altered by exposure to smoke.

glycosides can play a role in the expression of smoke-taint in berries and wine.
glycosylated compounds are important in smoke-taint expression.
